figures.alt: Engraving of armed Spanish men on a shore receiving gifts from Indigenous people, with ships at anchor and a cross being raised
figures.caption: Engraving by Theodor de Bry, 1594, showing Columbus's landing on Hispaniola

books.section: Topic 1.3 European exploration in the Americas
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

primary_sources: Theodor de Bry, engraving of Columbus's landing (1594)

options.text: The encounters mixed gift-giving with armed presence and religious claiming from the start
The encounters were battles in which the Spanish immediately attacked every Indigenous group they met
options.misconception: Reads a battle into the scene; the image shows gifts being offered, not fighting.

options.text: The encounters were peaceful exchanges between equals with no show of force
options.misconception: Ignores the armed men and the cross; the image shows force and claiming alongside the gifts.

options.text: The encounters were arranged by the pope, who sent priests to greet each landing party
options.misconception: No pope arranged the landings; the encounters happened on the shore between sailors and Indigenous peoples.

rationales.general:
1. Look at the foreground. Indigenous people approach carrying gifts, including gold objects.
2. Look at who else stands there. Armed Spanish men, and behind them a cross being raised on the beach.
3. Ask what the three parts add up to. Gifts, weapons, and a cross in one scene mean exchange, force, and claiming together.
4. Rule out the single stories. The scene is neither pure peace, nor pure battle, nor a papal ceremony.
Remember: when one image holds gifts and guns together, the encounter held both.
rationales.A: Gifts are offered in the foreground while armed men stand ready and a cross is raised behind them. The image holds exchange, force, and claiming in a single scene.
rationales.B: The image shows gifts being offered, not fighting. No battle is taking place on this shore.
rationales.C: The image shows armed men and a cross being raised, not only gifts. Force and claiming stand beside the exchange.
rationales.D: No pope arranged the landings. The encounters happened on the shore, between sailors and the Indigenous peoples they met.

stem: The engraving shows Indigenous people approaching the Spanish with gifts while armed Spanish men stand on the shore and a cross is raised behind them. Which claim about the first encounters between Europeans and Indigenous peoples is best supported by this image?

stimulus.source_note: Engraving by Theodor de Bry, 1594, public domain (Wikimedia Commons); de Bry never visited the Americas.
stimulus.text: Engraving by Theodor de Bry, 1594, showing Columbus's landing. In the foreground, Spanish men in armor stand on the shore as Indigenous people approach carrying gifts, including gold objects. Behind them, Spanish ships lie at anchor and more men raise a cross on the beach.
